ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows five circular disks, of different sizes, which is consistent with the textual information of the problem. The problem requires using three of the disks to build a tower, and the smaller disk must be placed above the larger disk. For any 3 disks selected, since their sizes are all different, there is only one stacking order that satisfies the rule: the largest is at the bottom, the middle-sized one is in the middle, and the smallest is at the top. Therefore, the number of towers is equal to the number of combinations of choosing 3 from 5 different disks, namely C(5,3)=5!/(3!2!)=10.

method.method_draft: Read that there are 5 discs, all different sizes, and that the tower must use exactly 3 discs with smaller discs always on top of bigger discs. Since any chosen set of 3 discs has only one valid stacking order: largest at bottom, middle-sized in middle, smallest on top. Therefore the number of towers equals the number of ways to choose 3 discs from 5: C(5,3)=10.
